entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: You kept the session short today, and short is what makes it repeatable. That repetition is what turns an intention into an identity.

suggestions.explanation: A version too small to fail is what builds the consistency to scale from.
suggestions.text: Do a two-minute version tomorrow before breakfast.

why: A straightforwardly faithful output. Anchors the top of both scales; a judge that scores this below 5 has a false-positive problem that makes every other number it produces unreadable.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: You relied on willpower this evening where your surroundings could have done the work instead.

suggestions.explanation: Making the wanted behaviour easy and the unwanted one hard is the point of environment design.
suggestions.text: Put the phone in a drawer and leave the book on the sofa cushion.

why: The one asymmetry LENS's grounding definition has and a generic faithfulness metric does not: a suggestion's ACTION is supposed to be a concrete tactic absent from the principles, because translating a principle into a next step is the job. Only the reflection and the explanation must stay accurate. A judge that deducts here would score correct output as unfaithful, which is the stated reason Ragas is not the primary metric.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: Consistency rather than scale is what held the morning together, and the smaller version is the one that repeats.

suggestions.explanation: Scale comes after the streak, not before it.
suggestions.text: Keep tomorrow's run at ten minutes.

why: Deliberately unspecific. Vagueness is not hallucination -- a judge that conflates 'said little' with 'invented something' will flag the pipeline's most cautious and most correct outputs.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: Every repetition of the shorter run casts a vote for the kind of person who runs, and after enough votes that becomes simply who you are.

suggestions.explanation: Each repetition is a vote for the identity rather than for the result.
suggestions.text: Run the ten-minute version again tomorrow.

why: Rubric point 4: every claim is traceable, but 'becomes simply who you are' pushes the identity principle further than the summary states. Authored to sit between 5 and 3 so faithfulness kappa has to resolve adjacent grades rather than opposite ends.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: Because surroundings matter more than willpower, the hour on the sofa was not really a choice you made at all.

suggestions.explanation: Changing the surroundings is a stronger lever than deciding to try harder.
suggestions.text: Move the charger out of the living room tonight.

why: Rubric point 3: the principle says surroundings are a better lever than willpower; this inflates it into 'the choice was not yours at all'. An over-generalisation, not a fabrication -- so hallucination stays false and only faithfulness moves.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: Self-control runs lowest in the evening, which is why the reading did not happen and the run did.

suggestions.explanation: Setting the surroundings up in advance beats relying on willpower later.
suggestions.text: Leave the book out before the evening starts.

why: The hardest case in the set and the reason it exists. Self-control declining through the day is a real finding, plausibly true, and completely absent from the principles -- so faithfulness is 2 while hallucination is FALSE, because nothing was invented and nothing was attributed to the book. A judge that collapses 'unsupported' into 'hallucinated' fails here, and that failure is invisible on any set where the two always coincide.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: The shorter run still counted, and repeating it is what makes it mean something.

suggestions.explanation: Repeating the smaller version is a vote for being someone who runs.
suggestions.text: Do the ten-minute version again tomorrow.

why: Groundedness 4: the suggestion is really an instance of start-small but is filed under identity-habits, where it still defensibly applies. Authored to test the adjacent grade on the groundedness scale.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: The evening went the way the room was arranged for it to go.

suggestions.explanation: Understanding the motivation is what makes the surroundings work.
suggestions.text: Write down three reasons the reading matters to you.

why: Groundedness 3: writing down reasons is a motivation tactic, and motivation is the lever the environment principle explicitly deprioritises. The reflection is clean, so this isolates the groundedness axis from the faithfulness one.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: The day had a shape to it, and small changes are what shift that shape.

suggestions.explanation: Staying hydrated steadies the mood that habits depend on.
suggestions.text: Drink more water through the afternoon.

suggestions.explanation: Social contact makes the rest of the week easier to face.
suggestions.text: Call a friend at the weekend.

suggestions.explanation: Tracking the conditions helps explain how the day went.

why: Groundedness 1, the floor. Three plausible-sounding wellness suggestions, none of which has anything to do with the principle it cites. Nothing is factually invented, so a judge keyed only on hallucination scores this clean.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: The book reports that ninety-two percent of people who start with a two-minute version stick with the habit for a year, which is roughly where you are.

suggestions.explanation: Small versions build the consistency larger ones depend on.
suggestions.text: Keep tomorrow's session to two minutes.

why: A fabricated number attributed to the book. No summary in the fixture set contains data of any kind, so this is unambiguous, and the suggestion itself is fine -- which keeps groundedness at 5 and stops the three rubric fields from moving as one block.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: A study by Dr Halvorsen in the book found that two-minute habits survive four times as often as ambitious ones.

suggestions.explanation: A version too small to fail is what the streak is built from.
suggestions.text: Shrink tomorrow's run to two minutes.

why: An invented researcher and an invented finding. Same rubric point as invented-statistic but a different surface form, so a judge that pattern-matches on digits rather than on attribution is caught.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: The book calls this “the plateau of latent potential”, which is where the shorter sessions have put you.

suggestions.text: Hold the habit at ten minutes for another week.

why: A short quoted phrase attributed to the book that appears nowhere in the principles. Under the fifteen-word cap, so every rule check passes it -- the quote limits protect against copyright exposure, not against invention, and only the judge can catch this one.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: The book argues you should begin with the most demanding version of a habit, because starting small teaches you to settle for less.

suggestions.explanation: Beginning at full scale is what the book recommends over easing in.
suggestions.text: Run five miles tomorrow rather than one.

why: States the opposite of what start-small says, and the suggestion follows the inversion. Faithfulness and groundedness both drop, which is the realistic correlated failure -- the set needs some of these or kappa is computed only on cases where the fields move independently.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: The book's four-hour rule for deep work says you cannot concentrate for more than four hours a day, so the length of the session was already right.

suggestions.explanation: The book's four-hour ceiling on concentration sets the size of the block.

why: A real idea from elsewhere attributed to this book. Nothing in the fixture set mentions concentration limits, so this is misattribution rather than error -- the failure mode a reader is least likely to notice, because the claim is true.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: You noticed the routine held on the days the setup was already done.

suggestions.explanation: Identity-based habits are about arranging your surroundings so the wanted choice is the easy one.
suggestions.text: Lay the running clothes out tonight.

why: The reflection is entirely sound, so faithfulness stays at 5 while the explanation misdescribes identity-habits as being about surroundings -- an idea attributed to the book that is not in it, so hallucination is true even at faithfulness 5. Authored specifically to break the assumption that the flag tracks the faithfulness score.

entries.action: Went for a run but cut it down to ten minutes because of the time
Meant to read but ended up scrolling on the sofa for an hour

reflection: You noticed the routine held on the days the setup was already done.

suggestions.explanation: Making the wanted choice the easy one works better than relying on willpower.
suggestions.text: Lay the running clothes out tonight.

why: Isolates id-level citation checking. The explanation describes design-environment accurately and never names the principle in prose, so the ONLY defect is the cited id. This is the case that was caught 0/5 before principle_ids were added to the entailment prompt and 5/5 after; here it tests whether the judge can see an id error without a prose cue.
